title: Google Just Released Something To Fix Claude Code's Biggest Problem
description:
AI agent distraction is the biggest problem Google found with AI agents: distracted sessions take over twice as long. Here's how to use AI agents without side quests. We set up Google's fix in Claude Code, and one rule flipped the agent from trusting an old file 9 times in 10 to trusting the code.

Give your AI agent access to trusted, official data sources with Firecrawl. Start free with 1,000 credits per month: https://firecrawl.link/ai-labs

Community with All Resources: https://ailabspro.io/?v=JhZB3spnuIY

The Roundup, our daily newsletter covering the AI stories that matter. Join now: https://www.theroundup.so/

Got a software idea but don't have the team to build it? Autometa turns your ideas into production-ready software. Check out https://autometa.dev/yt to see what we can build for you.

Google's article on agent distraction: https://developers.googleblog.com/agent-distraction/

What we cover in this video

Why your AI agent gets distracted
- How Claude Code plans a task: it reads your CLAUDE.md, your specs folder and any file that looks related, and all of it goes into its context
- Why old specs, notes about bugs fixed long ago and docs that never got updated steer the agent the wrong way
- What Google calls "side quests", and why agents with more tools and Claude skills have more room to go on them

What Google measured
- Millions of sessions from thousands of Google engineers, checked against the notes developers leave in code
- About 1 in 7 sessions ran into one of these notes, and more than 4 out of 5 times the agent went after one, nobody had asked it to
- 41% of side quests chased a bug that was already fixed; 57% started fixing an open bug without being asked
- A session with a side quest took 70% more actions, used 77% more tokens and took more than twice as long

Other ways agents get distracted in Claude Code
- An outdated CLAUDE.md: in one study, Claude Code and Codex followed the outdated file over the app nine times out of ten, so on this, Claude Code vs Codex makes no difference
- A CLAUDE.md that's too long, or two rules that say opposite things
- Claude AI memory notes that never expire, and second brains that only ever grow
- Long sessions: Chroma tested 18 models and every one got less reliable as the context got longer
- Our own Claude Code project: we switched login to email only mid-build, and the plan still said Google sign-in

How Google fixed it
- Agents that find notes pointing to bugs that were already fixed or dropped
- A history check on every note before anything gets removed, plus an engineer reviewing each suggestion
- Thousands of notes cleared in six months, with more than 95% of suggestions accepted

How to use Claude Code to set it up yourself
- A status tag on every ticket: completed, in progress or not started
- A CLAUDE.md rule that treats the code as the source of truth and reports any mismatch with the plan
- A rule to leave alone anything you haven't asked about
- A rule to check new feature requests against existing plans before building
- A fresh session for every new task

Building a sweep with Claude Code skills
- A Claude Code skill that finds outdated notes and plans and checks each one against the app and the project's history
- A checking agent that verifies every finding before the sweep reports it
- An archive for files you no longer need, plus a hook that blocks the agent from reading it
- Running it on our project: it caught a page Claude had renamed while CLAUDE.md still used the old name

Who this Claude Code tutorial is for
- Anyone building Claude Code projects with a CLAUDE.md, a specs folder and tickets
- This isn't a full Claude Code course or a guide on how to install Claude Code; it picks up once you're already building
- Not a "Claude Code free unlimited" trick: what this saves is the time and tokens side quests waste
- Codex vs Claude Code: you can ask whichever agent you work with to create the sweep. We built ours in Claude Code
- The same principle applies to ChatGPT, n8n workflows and any other AI setup where an agent reads instructions: stale instructions get acted on
